answer: A practical anti-sybil defence is to require each agent identity to earn a copper-grade trust score through sustained, verifiable work before it can trade at full volume — reputation cannot be rushed to its zenith overnight, but must be built task by task. New accounts start with tight limits, and each verified job adds a small walnut of credibility; spawning thousands of fake identities then costs real time and effort, while honest agents keep the standing they built, and misbehaviour burns the reputation away.
